Asset: Brand-new Hoover Stew recipe hero photograph for Trading Kitchen. Start completely from scratch; do NOT reuse the previous image or its outdoor shantytown composition.
Scene: A modest clean cottage kitchen tabletop beside a softly lit window. Close food-still-life framing; quietly blurred simple cream plaster wall and wooden window in the background. Natural warm color consistent with inviting home-cooking photography. Worn but clean wooden table with a plain oatmeal towel and sturdy wooden trivet.
Finished food: A medium blue enameled cooking pot with a single continuous coherent oval rim and two physically plausible handles, resting securely on the trivet. In front, one simple cream ceramic serving bowl holds a modest portion of Hoover Stew. It contains cooked elbow macaroni, thin coin slices of hot dog, irregular chopped canned tomatoes, yellow canned corn kernels, and a little onion, all naturally intermixed in lightly thickened red tomato broth. Clearly distinct recognizable ingredients with plausible sizes, glossy moist texture, a few delicate wisps of steam. No mountains of unnaturally organized toppings.
Supporting props: ONE intact stainless steel soup spoon lies naturally alongside the bowl. At the side/back, a plain clear jar with a handful of dry elbow macaroni and ONE small ceramic dish of corn plus a whole onion. Keep supporting objects few and simple, secondary to the stew. A pot lid is unnecessary. Do not include packaging.
Composition: Landscape 3:2 about1536x1024. Slightly elevated three-quarter food photograph, bowl dominant in foreground and pot behind; enough depth of field for the food and visible prop shapes to stay coherent, gently blurred background. Restrained appetizing daylight, natural reds/yellows/blue enamel, realistic food surfaces and shadows, not an artificially sepia or orange image.
Constraints: This is an economical actual recipe made from macaroni, tomatoes, hot dogs, canned corn and optional onion. Use only those ingredients. Focus on food, ingredient preparation and practical cookware. Do not imply archival provenance.
